This page is for contributors. It is the migration map of the frozen 1.x API
(the *baseline*, whose geometry package was `scgsim.sgb`): where its modules
and names live now, and who owns them. It does not list every current public
name; the [API index](../../reference/api-index.qmd) does.
Users import every public name from its package and need none of this; their
upgrade steps are in [Upgrade](../../guides/upgrade.qmd), and the public names
in the [API index](../../reference/api-index.qmd).

## Rules for moving a public name {#migration-rules}

- The package entry points are `scgsim.geometry`, `scgsim.palace`,
  `scgsim.aedt` and `scgsim.visualization`. Documented facades and declared
  exports are public; a module that happens to be importable is not.
- Each public name has one defining module, its responsibility owner, and the
  package facade re-exports it. A move leaves no second implementation and no
  compatibility wrapper at the old path, and a module declares only the names
  it defines.
- Q3D input-v1 and input-v2 are not revived: input-v3 on the SGB model is the
  Q3D request.
- `python -m scgsim.aedt.run`, its `main(argv)` and its `__main__` behavior
  stay: the generated handoff and EPR scripts call that command with their
  existing arguments. It is the supported CLI, not a legacy wrapper.
- AEDT receipts record the runtime source, schema
  `scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v30`: the import closure of the AEDT modules and
  both AEDT visualization loaders, computed on each use, with the SHA-256 of
  each file. A result recorded under an earlier runtime-source schema is
  refused and read with the SCGSim version that wrote it; old module paths are
  never mapped onto new ones. See the
  [runtime-source contract](../../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#runtime-source).

## Geometry names {#geometry-api}

The baseline `scgsim.sgb` facade maps to two surfaces. `scgsim.geometry` owns
source-facing planning, snapshots, normalized input records, the GDS and
stack-file adapter, vacuum preparation and detached summaries. The modules of
`scgsim.geometry.models` hold the input and record definitions. A layout enters
through `GeometryPlan` and the simulation classes; `build_sgb_geometry` in
`scgsim.geometry.sgb` builds the model from a prepared input and sits below that
entry, so a direct call with an input built by hand assumes what the entry
guarantees ([the supported entry](../../reference/supported-scope.qmd#supported-entry)).

| Baseline | Current owner | Names |
|---|---|---|
| `scgsim.sgb` | `scgsim.geometry` | `BoundaryCurveChainSpec`, `Coordinate`, `CurveKindLiteral`, `CurveOrientationLiteral`, `GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec`, `GeometryBuildInput`, `GeometryPlan`, `GeometryPlanSnapshot`, `InputSummary`, `LayoutPolygonSpec`, `PathInput`, `PolygonRing`, `PortSheetOverlapRecord`, `PortSheetRegionRecord`, `RouteLiteral`, `SemanticEntitySpec`, `SourceCurveSpec`, `VacuumRegionSpec`, `Vector3D`, `apply_vacuum_region_to_stack`, `build_gds_stack_geometry_input`, `summarize_geometry_input` |
| `scgsim.sgb.adapter` | `scgsim.geometry.source.adapter` | `build_gds_stack_geometry_input` |
| `scgsim.sgb.geometry_plan` | `scgsim.geometry.source.plan` | `GeometryPlan`, `GeometryPlanSnapshot` |
| `scgsim.sgb.models.common` | `scgsim.geometry.models.common` | `Coordinate`, `CurveKindLiteral`, `CurveOrientationLiteral`, `PathInput`, `PolygonRing`, `RouteLiteral`, `Vector3D`; and, imported from that module, `ConductorPartRoleLiteral`, `ConductorRepresentationLiteral`, `DEFAULT_INTERFACE_SOLVER_USE`, `HIGH_COUNT_LOCAL_CONDUCTOR_PART_ROLES`, `InterfaceKindLiteral`, `SolverUseLiteral` |
| `scgsim.sgb.models.input` | `scgsim.geometry.models.input` | `BoundaryCurveChainSpec`, `GdsBoundaryReconstructionSpec`, `GeometryBuildInput`, `LayoutPolygonSpec`, `SemanticEntitySpec`, `SourceCurveSpec`, `VacuumRegionSpec` |
| `scgsim.sgb.models.regions` | `scgsim.geometry.models.regions` | `PortSheetOverlapRecord`, `PortSheetRegionRecord` |
| `scgsim.sgb.summary` | `scgsim.geometry.source.summary` | `InputSummary`, `summarize_geometry_input` |
| `scgsim.sgb.vacuum` | `scgsim.geometry.source.vacuum` | `apply_vacuum_region_to_stack` |

Names that `scgsim.geometry` lists are imported from it; the other records from
their defining module. These baseline names have no supported import:

- the route builder of `scgsim.sgb`, `scgsim.sgb.pipeline`,
  `scgsim.sgb.planning`, `scgsim.sgb.export` and `scgsim.sgb.validation`:
  `SemanticGeometryBuilder`, `build_route_construction_plan`,
  `export_physical_group_records`, the stage functions
  (`plan_conductor_contact_patches`, `plan_cut_host_operations`,
  `plan_mm_contact_records`, `plan_route_construction_bodies`,
  `plan_route_surfaces`, `plan_route_tags`, `plan_route_volumes`,
  `plan_surface_partitions`, `recognize_route_interfaces`), every `validate_*`
  validator, the plan records (`BackendEntityTagRecord`,
  `ConstructionPlanRecord`, `CurvePlanRecord`, `CurveRefRecord`,
  `CutHostOperationRecord`, `FinalPhysicalGroupRecord`,
  `InnerPecVoidShellRecord`, `PointPlanRecord`, `RouteABConstructionPlanRecord`,
  `RouteABVolumePlanRecord`, `StructuredFinalPhysicalGroupRecord`,
  `SurfaceLoopRecord`, `SurfaceRefRecord`, `TagPlanRecord`, `VolumePlanRecord`)
  and the literals `DimensionLiteral`, `GmshDimTag`,
  `ROUTE_ALLOWED_REPRESENTATIONS`, `RUN_METADATA_DIR`,
  `SEMANTIC_GEOMETRY_METADATA_DIR`, `SurfaceLoopRoleLiteral`,
  `SurfaceOrientationLiteral` and `TagSourceKindLiteral`. A layout is built
  through `GeometryPlan` and `EigenmodeSim` or `ElectrostaticSim`; a prepared
  input of one's own through `build_sgb_geometry`;
- the component adapter, `scgsim.sgb.stack` and `scgsim.sgb.source_curves`:
  `build_gdsfactory_geometry_input`, `build_component_stack`,
  `bind_source_curves`. A component with a `component_semantics` schema 2
  declaration enters through `GeometryPlan`, which builds the stack from the
  PDK layer stack and carries the authored curve bindings itself;
- removed in 3.0.0rc3 with AEDT's own geometry builder:
  `scgsim.geometry.planning`, `scgsim.geometry.models.topology`
  (`InterfacePlanRecord`, `MMContactRecord`, `SurfacePlanRecord`) and the
  construction records `ConstructionBodyPlanRecord` and
  `SurfacePartitionRecord`.

Below the facade the modules carry responsibility names. The grid engine is
`scgsim.geometry.grid`, with `grid_cache`, `tagged_grid`, `tagged_grid_faces`,
`tagged_grid_operations` and `polygon_ops`; source preparation is
`scgsim.geometry.source`, with `normalization`, `occurrence` and
`plan_assembly`. Lumped elements are declared with `LumpedElement` and
`LumpedPort` and resolved into `LumpedElementRecord`s by
`scgsim.geometry.source.lumped_elements`; each simulation binds its sheets for
the rectangular partition with `RectangularJunctionSpec`,
`JunctionTerminalBinding` and `with_rectangular_junctions` from
`scgsim.geometry`, derived by `interpret_physical_geometry`; the shared contact service
(`JunctionContactRequest`, `junction_contact_inventory`) lives in
`scgsim.geometry.junctions.contact` and is not exported.

## AEDT names and module owners {#aedt-api-transaction-and-state-ownership}

Every public AEDT name below is exported by `scgsim.aedt`, except the CLI's
`main`, which stays in `scgsim.aedt.run`; the
[API index](../../reference/api-index.qmd) lists them. The baseline modules
map to their owners as follows; listing a module here does not make it public.

| Baseline | Current owner | Names |
|---|---|---|
| `scgsim.aedt.spec` | `scgsim.aedt.specs.common` | `AedtResources`, `PdkMaterial`, `TerminalPort`, `ModalPort`, `MatrixRunControl` |
| `scgsim.aedt.spec` | `scgsim.aedt.specs.hfss` | `FrequencySweepSpec`, `HfssRunControl`, `EigenmodeRunControl`, `HfssSpec`, `HfssEprSpec`, `HfssEprAnalysisSpec` |
| `scgsim.aedt.spec` | `scgsim.aedt.specs.q2d` | `Q2dRectangleSpec`, `Q2dConductorSpec`, `Q2dSpec` |
| `scgsim.aedt.spec` | `scgsim.aedt.specs.q3d` | `Q3dNetSpec`, `Q3dSpec` |
| `scgsim.aedt.spec` | `scgsim.aedt.specs.parse` | `AedtSpec`, `parse_aedt_spec` |
| `scgsim.aedt._epr_models` | `scgsim.aedt.epr.models` | `EprResult` |
| `scgsim.aedt._epr_models` | `scgsim.aedt.specs.epr` | `EprAnalysisRequest`, `ExpressionCacheConvergence`, `NativeExpressionDefinition`, `NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal`, `SavedSolution` |
| `scgsim.aedt.handoff` | `scgsim.aedt.preparation.handoff` | `HandoffPlan`, `prepare_handoff` |
| `scgsim.aedt.handoff` | `scgsim.aedt.preparation.geometry` | `prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry`, `prepare_hfss_eigenmode_from_geometry`, `prepare_q3d_from_geometry` |
| `scgsim.aedt.handoff` | `scgsim.aedt.epr.workflow` | `analyze_epr` |
| `scgsim.aedt.eigenmode` | `scgsim.aedt.eigenmode` | `EigenmodeSim` |
| `scgsim.aedt.resolve` | `scgsim.aedt.results.resolve` | `ResolvedRun`, `resolve_results` |
| `scgsim.aedt._epr_results` | `scgsim.aedt.epr.reanalysis` | `reanalyze_epr` |
| `scgsim.aedt._epr_results` | `scgsim.aedt.results.epr` | `resolve_epr_result`, `resolve_saved_solution` |
| `scgsim.aedt._epr_results`, `_presentation` | `scgsim.aedt.presentation.epr` | `plot_epr_result`, `show_epr` |
| `scgsim.aedt.run` | `scgsim.aedt.run` | `main` |
| (new in 3.0.0rc3) | `scgsim.aedt.preparation.sgb_model` | `PreparedSgbModel` |

The responsibility tree:

- `aedt.specs` owns the common, HFSS, Q2D and Q3D-v3 request records and the
  parsing of each family.
- `aedt.preparation` owns the SGB model for AEDT, the portable handoff that
  carries it and the membership of a handoff's files.
- `aedt.runtime.transaction` is the only owner of AEDT Desktop and of the
  receipt's state. Each family's runtime owns its native prepare, solve, export
  and readback; the shared native helper owns neither a family nor Desktop.
- `aedt.epr` owns the EPR models, source geometry, fields and cache, and the
  workflow. `aedt.results` owns the strict handoff and result resolution,
  provenance, convergence, matrices and the sealed EPR readers; results never
  start a solve.
- `aedt.presentation` owns display-only projections and plots, imported lazily
  so that strict result reading does not load them.

`EigenmodeSim` stays the mutable state owner of the plan, the EPR settings,
the preparation and the invalidation of a handoff; preparation helpers do not
take that state over. A transaction validates the request and its files,
writes the running receipt before PyAEDT or Desktop starts, runs one family
transaction, keeps what came back before Desktop is released, then seals any
saved EPR result. An earlier native or family error stays the primary error if
the release also fails; resolution checks returned files without running AEDT.
There is no shared simulation base class and no common physical-result model.

The documented baseline modules move as follows: `spec` to
`specs.common`, `specs.hfss`, `specs.q2d`, `specs.q3d` and `specs.parse`;
`handoff` splits among `preparation.handoff`, `preparation.geometry` and
`epr.workflow`; `eigenmode` stays the state-owning facade; `resolve` moves to
`results.resolve`; and `run.main` stays at `scgsim.aedt.run` as a thin delegate.
The importable but unexported `aedt.util` became an internal I/O module and has
no wrapper. Visualization imports PyAEDT constants from the spec owner without
making them public.

## Palace names {#palace-package-symbols}

`scgsim.palace` exports 42 names, grouped here by defining module:

| Defining module | Responsibility | Names |
|---|---|---|
| `scgsim.palace.simulation` | The three simulation classes on one shared core | `ElectrostaticSim`, `EigenmodeSim`, `DrivenSim` |
| `scgsim.palace.simulation.drc` | The two-stage layout check, also run by `mesh()` | `SimulationDrcError`, `SimulationDrcReport`, `StageResult` |
| `scgsim.palace.config.convergence` | The criteria of a convergence declaration | `Capacitance`, `Criterion`, `CriterionGroup`, `ErrorIndicator`, `ModeFrequency`, `SurfaceEpr` |
| `scgsim.contracts.palace_convergence` | The plan, check and verdict of a declaration | `ConvergenceCheck`, `ConvergencePlan`, `ConvergenceVerdict` |
| `scgsim.palace.results.convergence` | How the solver ended | `SolverEnd` |
| `scgsim.palace.results.resolved_records` | The checked records of a returned run | `PalaceCost`, `PalacePerformance`, `PalaceProvenance`, `PalaceReturnedReceipt`, `ParsedTable` |
| `scgsim.palace.reports.resolved_result` | The resolved result a user holds, with its views | `ResolvedPalaceResult`, `resolve_palace_result` |
| `scgsim.palace.results.epr`, `scgsim.palace.results.epr_records` | Detached EPR values and offline reanalysis | `PalaceEprResult`, `epr_result`, `reanalyze_epr`, `resolve_epr_result` |
| `scgsim.palace.reports.epr` | The plot of a detached EPR result | `show_epr` |
| `scgsim.palace.results.driven`, `scgsim.palace.results.driven_records` | The detached result of a Driven run: its S-parameters, Surface EPR and adaptive sampling | `PalaceDrivenResult`, `DrivenSurfaceEpr`, `AdaptiveSampling` |
| `scgsim.semantics.s_parameters` | The S-parameter record every driven solver returns, and its Touchstone writer | `SParameters`, `SParameterPort` |
| `scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records` | Detached records the reports read | `PalaceFailureDiagnosis`, `PalaceResultSelection`, `PassCostRecord`, `SurfaceMarginEprRecord`, `SurfaceMarginEprSeriesSnapshot` |
| `scgsim.palace.reports.reports`, `scgsim.palace.reports.trust`, `scgsim.palace.reports.views` | The trust, physics and benchmark views | `inspect_run_trustworthiness`, `PalaceTrustReport`, `PhysicsQuantitiesReport`, `SimulationBenchmarkReport` |
| `scgsim.palace.reports.driven` | The trust and physics views of a Driven run | `DrivenTrustReport`, `DrivenPhysicsReport` |

`scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records` also defines `AmrPassSnapshot`,
`SurfaceEprRecord` and `SurfaceEprSeriesSnapshot`, which the package does not
export.

## Palace submodules {#palace-direct-submodule-exports}

The baseline's Palace submodules declared their own `__all__`. A name that
`scgsim.palace` exports is imported from it; the others have no supported
import, and the table says what replaces them:

| Baseline import | Import now | Defining module |
|---|---|---|
| `scgsim.palace.electrostatic` (`ElectrostaticSim`) | `scgsim.palace` | `scgsim.palace.simulation.electrostatic` |
| `scgsim.palace.eigenmode` (`EigenmodeSim`) | `scgsim.palace` | `scgsim.palace.simulation.eigenmode` |
| `scgsim.palace.handoff` (`HandoffPlan`, `HandoffProfile`, `prepare_handoff`) | None of the three is exported. A handoff is prepared with the simulation's method `sim.prepare_handoff(profile=..., executable=..., resources=...)`, which returns the `HandoffPlan`; `HandoffProfile` is the literal type of its `profile` values (`"direct-local"`, `"slurm-single-node"`, `"slurm-multi-node"`). | `scgsim.palace.run.handoff` (internal) |
| `scgsim.palace.resolve` (`PalaceCost`, `PalacePerformance`, `PalaceProvenance`, `PalaceReturnedReceipt`, `ParsedTable`, `ResolvedPalaceResult`, `resolve_palace_result`) | `scgsim.palace`, all seven | The records in `scgsim.palace.results.resolved_records`; `ResolvedPalaceResult` and `resolve_palace_result` in `scgsim.palace.reports.resolved_result` |
| `scgsim.palace.report` (`PalaceFailureDiagnosis`, `PalaceResultSelection`, `PalaceTrustReport`, `PassCostRecord`, `PhysicsQuantitiesReport`, `inspect_run_trustworthiness`) | `scgsim.palace` | `inspect_run_trustworthiness` in `scgsim.palace.reports.reports`, `PalaceTrustReport` in `scgsim.palace.reports.trust`, `PhysicsQuantitiesReport` in `scgsim.palace.reports.views`, the records in `scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records` |
| `scgsim.palace.report` (`AmrPassSnapshot`) | Not exported: an internal record of the trust report's passes | `scgsim.palace.results.inspection_records` (internal) |
| `scgsim.palace._epr_results` (private) | Its supported names, re-exported by `scgsim.palace`; the old path is no compatibility surface | `scgsim.palace.results` |

## Visualization names {#visualization-symbols}

`scgsim.visualization` exports exactly `GeometryPreview`,
`GeometryPreviewArtifact`, `inspect_aedt_geometry` and
`inspect_palace_geometry`.

| Names | Defining module | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `GeometryPreview`, `GeometryPreviewArtifact` | `scgsim.visualization.preview` | The source-bound preview and its returned contact sheet or unavailable mode |
| `inspect_palace_geometry` | `scgsim.visualization.loaders.palace` | Read the Palace mesh, manifest, index map and config into preview modes |
| `inspect_aedt_geometry` | `scgsim.visualization.loaders.aedt` | Bind the AEDT receipt and read back the solver-assigned geometry; a raw `.aedt` file needs `aedt_version` and the design, a run folder uses its recorded version |
| Scene records and rendering | `scgsim.visualization.scene`, `scgsim.visualization.rendering` | Scene construction and rendering, without solver physics or status |
| Loader file helpers | `scgsim.visualization.loaders.common` | JSON, hash and confined-path reading shared by the loaders |

Preview files and their manifest stay outside solver and handoff identity.
Palace previews keep high-order cell connectivity and node coordinates; source
curves and native curve facts stay in the mesh manifest and the detached mesh
summary.

## Shared presentation {#shared-presentation}

The baseline's private `scgsim._notebook_presentation` held formatting helpers
that geometry and AEDT share. They are now `scgsim.presentation.notebook`. The
helpers own no Palace or AEDT projection, calculation or result status, and
the move makes none of their names public.

## The AEDT `modeling` value {#solidthin-film-request-migration}

Every Q3D and HFSS 3D request names `modeling="solid"` or
`modeling="thin_film"`, with no default; an absent or other value is never
inferred. It chooses the SGB route the model is built on: `thin_film` is Route
A, `solid` Route C. A request payload without `modeling`, or one written for
AEDT's own geometry builder, was written by an earlier SCGSim and is refused.
The physical layers are the plan's `PhysicalLayerDeclaration` records in the
one `LayerStack` coordinate system
([physical representation](../../reference/specs/physical-representation.qmd));
a film's original normal thickness travels in
`physical_dimensions["normal_thickness_um"]`, and the film thickness output
reports it without recomputing it. The earlier `PhysicalLayerSpec(...)` record
is removed. Q2D and Palace take no `modeling`. The full transform, materials,
terminals and failures are in the
[AEDT solid and thin-film contract](../../reference/specs/aedt-runtime.qmd#aedt-solid-thin-film).
